title: What comes next?
cues: The cat sat on the...
Show the unfinished sentence and hold on the blank.
You might say mat, floor, or chair. Moon is possible, but it feels less likely.
Reveal four example probabilities in descending order.
Now imagine the story takes place in a rocket. The same ending can have different odds when the context changes.
Change the context and animate the same bars to new probabilities.
A large language model learns patterns that help it predict what text might come next.
Hold on the distribution before carrying the sentence into tokenization.

title: From text to numbers
cues: Before the network can do arithmetic on this sentence, it needs a way to turn text into numbers.
Bring the sentence into three connected tiles.
A tokenizer splits text into pieces called tokens. A piece can be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or include a space.
Separate the tiles and mark leading spaces.
Each piece gets an ID from a vocabulary. The ID is just a lookup number, like an index in a table.
Reveal example IDs beneath tokens.
The ID selects a learned list of numbers. This list is a vector, and we call it an embedding.
Run a pulse from the selected ID to one row of numbers.

title: A space of representations
cues: What can a list of numbers tell us? Imagine using just three numbers as coordinates, so we can put each item somewhere in space.
Move from the lookup row to a rotating Three.js coordinate grid.
Cat and dog often occur in similar contexts. The model can learn patterns from that, and related tokens can end up near one another.
Light the cat, dog, and animal points and draw their connections.
Car occurs in different contexts, so here we place it farther away.
Reveal the separate car point.
These are illustrative positions. Real embeddings have many more dimensions, and their coordinates are learned during training.
Label the projection as illustrative and hold before the context example.

title: Put context to work
cues: The animal didn't cross the street because it was tired. What does it refer to?
Reveal the sentence and isolate it.
The starting vector for it cannot tell us. The model needs a way to pull information from earlier tokens.
Trace links backward from it, with stronger emphasis on animal.
Attention weighs how relevant earlier positions are for the current one. Then it mixes information from those positions.
Animate strength-weighted contributions converging on a new vector.
The current token creates a query. Earlier positions supply keys for matching, and values supply the information that gets mixed.
Sequence Query, Key, then Value labels and corresponding visual focus.
That gives it a context-sensitive representation. Attention is one part of a Transformer.
Hold the updated vector and carry it into the first layer.

title: Inside the Transformer
cues: One pass can pull in useful clues. A Transformer stacks layers so each layer can build on representations made by the previous one.
Fly through a stack of translucent planes with token traces.
Attention mixes information across positions. A feed-forward network then transforms each position separately.
Light the two sub-stages in turn.
Residual connections carry information forward. Normalization helps keep the numerical scale manageable.
Highlight a bypass and a stabilizing stage.
Learned numbers called weights determine how these operations transform the vectors. The work is spread across many numbers and operations.
Display changing vector components across layers.

title: How the weights learn
cues: During pretraining, take a piece of text. Let the model predict the next token, then compare its prediction with the token that actually occurred.
Start the training loop with text, prediction, and target.
A loss measures the mismatch. Backpropagation computes gradients, which tell us how small changes to weights would affect that loss.
Follow the loss with a reversed gradient path.
An optimizer uses those gradients to adjust weights. Repeat across enormous amounts of training text.
Advance weight updates and loop through new examples.
Later, instruction tuning can train on example responses. Preference-based training can favor responses people or other evaluators rate more highly.
Reveal the stages in order.
During ordinary use, the learned weights stay fixed.
Freeze the weight indicators.

title: From prompt to response
cues: Back to our cat. The prompt becomes token IDs, then embeddings. The Transformer turns those vectors into representations informed by context.
Send a pulse through the first four pipeline stages.
The model produces a score for each possible next token. A softmax turns the scores into probabilities.
Reveal scores and convert them to a distribution.
A selection rule picks a token. Sampling settings can make lower-probability choices more or less likely.
Adjust example probabilities and highlight the selected token.
The chosen token joins the context. The process runs again, one token at a time.
Append successive tokens and trace the loop back to the input.

title: The mental model
cues: An LLM is a neural network trained to transform context into predictions about what comes next.
Zoom out from token generation to the full pipeline.
Learning patterns across enormous amounts of data builds representations that can support language generation, problem solving, and many other tasks.
Trace from training into weights and from weights into inference.
Likely text can still be wrong.
Hold the full system with a concise factual accuracy reminder.
